title: Comparatives and superlatives
subtitle: Comparing two things, and picking one out of a group

blocks.text: We use comparatives to compare things, people or actions that are different. The comparative form is often followed by **than**.

rows.example: My new job is **more enjoyable** than my old one. I'd like you to get to the office **earlier** tomorrow.

rows.use: one syllable ending in -e · late → later
one syllable ending in vowel + consonant · big → bigger
rows.example: This bag is **bigger** than that one.

rows.use: two syllables ending in -y · pretty → prettier
two or more syllables · interesting → more/less interesting
rows.example: This book is **more interesting** than the film.
well → **better** · badly → **worse** · near → **nearer** · late → **later** · fast → **faster** · early → **earlier** · far → **farther/further**

items: My working day is **longer than** it used to be.

blocks.text: We use superlatives to compare one member of a group of things, people or actions with the whole group. We usually use **the** before the superlative form.

rows.example: Out of all the jobs in the company, John's is **the hardest**. The person who does **best** will get a pay rise.

rows.use: one syllable ending in -e · late → latest
rows.example: This is **the latest** train we can catch.

rows.use: one syllable ending in vowel + consonant · big → biggest
rows.example: That's **the biggest** pizza I've ever seen.

rows.use: two syllables ending in -y · pretty → prettiest
rows.example: Which is **the prettiest** village on the coast?

rows.use: two or more syllables · interesting → most/least interesting
rows.example: This is **the most interesting** talk of the day.
well → **best** · badly → **worst** · near → **nearest** · late → **latest** · fast → **fastest** · early → **earliest** · far → **farthest/furthest**

items: Today was **the worst** day since I started working there.

exercises.title: A · Comparative form
exercises.instruction: Complete using the comparative form of the words in brackets.

items.prompt: Wait! Your bicycle is ___ than mine! (fast)
Phew! It's much ___ than it was yesterday, isn't it? (hot)
I think you look ___ when you wear your hair up. (pretty)
The price of batteries has gone up. They're a lot ___ than last time. (expensive)
Angus hasn't been practising the piano and he's got a lot ___ . (bad)
His new film is much ___ than his last one. I loved that one! (entertaining)
Tell us another joke — but a ___ one this time! That one took forever! (short)
I didn't win the lottery. Maybe I'll be ___ next time. (lucky)
The Russian athlete threw the discus ___ than all the others and won gold. (far)
I think these biscuits are even ___ than the last ones you made! (nice)

exercises.title: B · Correct the comparative
exercises.instruction: The words in bold in each sentence are wrong. Write the correct word.

items.prompt: We lost the match because we played **badly** than the other team did.
It rains a lot in England, so the countryside is a lot **green** than in Greece.
You gave Sarah a really small piece of cake — and you've given me even **little**!
I must have lost weight. These jeans seem **large** than they were before.
I got to the party **early** than everyone else, so I had to wait.
I hear her new CD is **good** than her last one. What do you think?
Our cat seems to be getting **fat** every day — maybe she should go on a diet!
I'm disappointed. I think you could have done a lot **well** on this test.

exercises.title: C · Opposite comparatives
exercises.instruction: Rewrite the sentences using the correct comparative form of the words in the box.

items.prompt:
Joshua is much taller than Alex.
Alex is ___ .
acceptedAnswers: Alex is much shorter than Joshua.
Alex is much shorter than Joshua

items.prompt:
Theresa is more confident than Amy.
Amy is a lot ___ .
acceptedAnswers: Amy is a lot less confident than Theresa.
Amy is a lot less confident than Theresa

items.prompt:
Your house is further from the school than mine.
My house is ___ .
acceptedAnswers: nearer to the school than yours
closer to the school than yours
My house is nearer to the school than yours.
My house is nearer to the school than yours

items.prompt:
Jude is less happy than Andy about the decision.
Andy is ___ .
acceptedAnswers: happier than Jude about the decision
happier about the decision than Jude
Andy is happier than Jude about the decision.
Andy is happier than Jude about the decision

items.prompt:
Bill is thinner than Simon.
Simon is ___ .

Terry is older than Sarah-Jane.
Sarah-Jane is ___ .

Patricia is better than her sister on the clarinet.
Patricia's sister is ___ .
acceptedAnswers: worse than Patricia on the clarinet
worse on the clarinet than Patricia
Patricia's sister is worse than Patricia on the clarinet.
Patricia's sister is worse than Patricia on the clarinet

items.prompt:
The houses here are uglier than in my grandparents' village.
The houses in my grandparents' village are ___ .
acceptedAnswers: more beautiful than the houses here
The houses in my grandparents' village are more beautiful than here.
The houses in my grandparents' village are more beautiful than here

exercises.title: D · Superlatives
exercises.instruction: Complete using the correct form of the words in the box.

items.prompt: This really is the ___ song I've ever heard! It's terrible!
Ivy is the ___ woman I know. She'll do anything for anybody.
Listen! I promise you, this is the ___ joke ever! Well, a man goes into a shop …
Mmm! This is the ___ soup you've made so far.
What's the ___ thing about English grammar for you?
Ben appeared and he was carrying the ___ present I'd ever seen. It was huge!
We had a competition to see who could swim the ___ .
Sandra told us the ___ ghost story she could, and it was really frightening!

exercises.title: E · Jobs compared
exercises.instruction: Complete using the correct form of the words in brackets.

items.prompt: I think this is the (1) ___ job I've ever had. (bad)
My last job was much (2) ___ than this one. (good)
I had a lot (3) ___ work there and my boss was really nice. (little)
My boss here is the (4) ___ in the whole firm. (strict)
The working day is (5) ___ than in my last job, too. (long)
The (6) ___ thing about it is that the office is closer to my house than the old one. (good)
The office is (7) ___ to my house than the old one. (close)
At least now I get home (8) ___ than I used to. (early)

Tortoise: 'I walk the (2) ___ of all.'

Second boy: 'I ran (7) ___ than everyone except him.'
Second boy: 'They both ran (8) ___ than me.'
